title: Quantitative stabilization for functorial hypercohomology
statement: For canonical derived pullback maps P on bounded-below complexes of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], specified by the adjunction unit and derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], there exist global Cartan-Eilenberg presentations T, page maps M, thresholds R(X,K,q,n), and stable-page-to-graded-piece isomorphisms eInf, with all first-page, filtered abutment, identity and composition equations of [lem-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-e1-pullback-functorial]. Moreover, for every lower bound a with K^s=0 for s<a, R(X,K,q,n) <= max(1,max(q-a+2,n-q+2)). The global presentations and maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation]. No diagram, colimit, or coordinate reindexing is involved.

proof.text: Obtain supported presentations D, spectral-sequence maps M, and stationary comparisons eSupported on support-admissible pages from lem-weil-pbc-supported-resolution-maps.

For each X,K,q,n, define admissible(r) by existence of a lower support bound a with max(1,q-a+2,n-q+2)≤r. K.property supplies a strict lower bound; isZero_of_isStrictlyGE gives zero terms below it. Casting the displayed positive maximum to a natural number proves an admissible natural page exists. Let R be Nat.find of this predicate. Nat.find_spec and upward closure give admissible(r) whenever R≤r. Nat.find_min' and the nonnegative integer-to-natural cast show R≤max(1,q-a+2,n-q+2) for every valid a. Define eInf by restricting eSupported along this proved implication.

Choose a resolution comparison j over v using surjectivity of precomposition in the homotopy category into the target K-injective resolution. Build the chain map w by the global-sections inverse-image unit and Γ(j); verify its differential square using unit naturality. Use the supported construction for filtration-step maps t and ht. The K-injective pullback abutment theorem and hP identify its concrete resolution-cohomology map with P. Monicity of each filtration inclusion then proves hc. Apply the supported stable-page equation at the two admissible-page witnesses supplied by R≤r.

Use derivedEtaleCohomology_pullback_laws for the P identity and composition equations. Spectral-sequence morphisms are determined by their first page: induct on r≥1, using the structure isomorphisms to homology and cancellation of their homs. In nonnegative complementary degree compute M identity and composition from hE and cohomologyPullbackFunctorial, with cohomologyMap_map for naturality in v. In negative complementary degree use D.negative to equate all maps from the zero object.

proof_origin.place: Lean reduction: support-controlled construction; least admissible threshold; K-injective abutment identification and first-page functoriality. Reuses the library pullback-map and functoriality proof arguments.

mathlib_searches.results: UNAVAILABLE: Internal Server Error; local source grep and LeanFinder used instead.

mathlib_searches.query: A lower bounded complex has uniform stable hypercohomology spectral sequence pages natural for pullback
mathlib_searches.results: DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isGE; CochainComplex.cm5b; CochainComplex.isZero_of_isLE. These are support and resolution lemmas, not the functorial page package.

Mathlib SpectralSequence.Basic has page functors and hom_ext but no coordinate-swap functor. IsColimit.isZero_pt and isColimitOfPreserves prove the colimit bound. Existing pullback presentations have object-dependent thresholds without a uniform estimate.

mathlib_searches.query: The first hypercohomology spectral sequence of a complex zero below a stabilizes at bidegree (q,n-q) once r exceeds both q-a and n-q+1
mathlib_searches.results: Independent second reader: CochainComplex.isZero_of_isGE/isLE and derived analogues are vanishing tools only. HypercohomologyConvergence uses truncation couples, not the supplied termwise presentations. FilteredResolutionMaps has thresholds without the quantitative estimate; no exact match.
